Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over. I’ve pulled together concise answers below and looped in Kim (security & compliance) and Priyom (product ops) for any specific operational notes or follow-ups.

Quick summary (full answers attached in a one-page matrix):
1) Data residency: Hosted API customer input is stored in the region selected at account creation (US or EU). By default accounts created from the US region keep data in US-backed storage; we do not shard customer request payloads to other geographies unless region pinning to EU is requested.

2) Retention windows (defaults for hosted API):
   - Request payloads and generated responses: retained 30 days by default (configurable per customer contract).
   - Runtime/debug logs (expanded traces used for incident triage): retained 14 days, encrypted at rest.
   - Audit logs (auth events, admin actions): retained 365 days (we provide export options).
   - Backups/snapshots of underlying data store: retained 90 days; snapshots are region-scoped.

3) Purge process:
   - Customer initiates via Support portal or signed DSAR; we schedule a tenant purge job.
   - Standard hosted purge timeline: up to 72 hours to remove active data, plus up to 14 days to scrub cached artifacts and asynchronous backups (90-day snapshot deletion follows backup retention policy unless an accelerated deletion addendum is in place).

4) Geo-replication and deletion:
   - Snapshots/backups are region-scoped by default; we don’t replicate hosted customer data across regions without explicit customer onboarding for multi-region failover. If replication exists per contract, we follow the same purge workflow across replicas and provide deletion attestations.

I’ve attached a compact matrix and a sample deletion attestation template. Kim/Priyom — can you confirm the backup replication language and whether we can offer a 30-day accelerated-snapshot-delete addendum for their RFP?

Best,

Ben — adding a few operational clarifications to make Elena’s team comfortable:

- Storage and encryption: All hosted-customer data at rest is encrypted with customer-specific keys managed in our KMS. For enterprise customers we support customer-managed CMKs via AWS KMS or partner HSMs.
- Logs separation: Debug/traces used for model performance debugging are stored separately from tenant request logs; we tag traces with an internal token that can be scrubbed as part of a purge.
- KV/prefix caches: Short-lived caches (used to accelerate repeated prompts) are ephemeral and have TTLs < 24 hours by default; these caches do not persist to backups.
- Attestation: After a purge we provide a signed attestation noting which object IDs were removed and the job run id. The attestation is delivered via secure link and recorded in the customer’s audit log.

Priyom — for their RFP note we can offer: 30-day default retention, 14-day debug retention, 90-day snapshot retention with optional accelerated snapshot deletion (30-day) as a contractual addendum for an additional compliance fee. Also recommend we include a bullet about deletion of third-party telemetry (we can scope this per contract).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Engagement, Redwood Inference

- Default residency: US (accounts created via the US onboarding flow). EU residency available on sign-up or via a migration with a two-week coordination window.
